name: Carta Online
author: cartaonline

sections.description:
The Carta Online Course Administrator WordPress plugin enables integration, publishing and processing of your offerings in Carta.
With the co-offerlist shortcode your offerings can easily be integrated in your existing WordPress web pages.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/plugin-name directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Use the ‘carta online’ screen to configure the plugin
  4. Direct download link: Carta Online plugin

Detailed installation instructions can be found at Carta Online
sections.faq:
Does the plugin work without a valid Carta License?

No, you need to obtain a Carta Online API key to use the plugin. A demo site is available on request. Send an e-mail with your project details to info@cartaonline.nl to obtain a demo API-KEY.

Can I hide the thumbnail picture or location in the generated list of offerings?

Yes, You can. You can add styling to the plugin, or to your theme. If needed every rendered object can be styled individually, by type or by usage. Use the styling option display:none to hide the disable unneeded elements.
sections.changelog:
2.19.0-beta1

  • Page caching: the plugin now decides per page whether it may be cached, instead of switching caching off for the entire site. A page that shows offer data is only declared cacheable when this site receives webhooks and the plugin can clear the page cache again; pages without offer data are left alone. The old “Session cache limiter” setting is renamed “Never allow page caching (legacy)”, still works, and can only ever make the decision stricter. It will be removed in a following release.
  • Page caching: when an offering changes, the plugin clears exactly the pages that show it in WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache and Nginx Helper, and offers an action plus HTTP PURGE endpoints for anything else. Every attempt and its result per cache is visible on Tools > Carta Online aanbod, and a failed purge makes the plugin stop declaring offer pages cacheable rather than serving old prices.
  • Offer pages no longer set cookies. Filter selections live in the address bar instead, so a filtered list is now linkable, bookmarkable, crawlable, and the back button works. The previous design also meant no page cache would ever store an offer page, and one visitor’s filter could have been served to the next.
  • Detail pages: title, description and canonical link now come from the local cache, so the head of a course page is complete even when the portal is unreachable, and every course has its own canonical instead of all of them sharing one. Two API calls per pageview are gone.
  • SEO: three optional lines per course in Carta (SEO_Titel, SEO_Omschrijving, SEO_Zoekwoorden) fill the page title, the description and the keywords. Empty falls back to the course name and summary, cut on a word boundary. The keywords tag is only emitted when it is actually filled; it used to contain the course name with its spaces replaced by commas. Yoast and Rank Math get these values through their own filters when active, instead of a second set of tags next to theirs.
  • Speed: rendering an offer list no longer calls the portal at all. Teacher lists, contacts, accreditations, public documents, teacher names, the company list and the portal version now come from the local cache, filled in the background. A list with teacher and price placeholders used to cost one call per row plus one per teacher.
  • Speed: with “special pages” enabled the rewrite rules were rebuilt on every single page view. That now happens on activation and when the setting changes.
  • Correctness: a course detail page for an unknown course now answers a real 404 (or a redirect when one is configured), instead of HTTP 200 with a JavaScript redirect that search engines read as a soft 404. A detail page without a course in the address does the same; that case emitted broken JavaScript and did nothing at all.
  • Correctness: the internal response cache moved from files to transients, so it works behind a load balancer and uses an object cache such as Redis when the host provides one. This also removes a bug where a left-over lock file could keep a cached response valid regardless of its age, which could show old data for as long as it lasted.
  • Editor: the offer list and the filter are now also available as blocks with labelled fields, so placing them no longer requires looking up shortcode attributes. Both render on the server, so the offerings stay visible to search engines.
  • Removed includes/co_datatable.php. It declared a directly-callable endpoint but blocked direct calls, so it has been unreachable for years.
  • Cache schema 1.4.0: two new tables for the reads that used to happen while rendering. Existing offerings are refreshed once in the background after the update.
  • SEO: a course detail page now also carries Open Graph tags and schema.org Course markup, both built from the local cache. A link shared on LinkedIn or WhatsApp shows the course with its own title, description and image instead of the generic detail page, and Google can show the course with its date, location and price. When Yoast or Rank Math is active they keep ownership of the Open Graph tags and receive the per-course values through their own filters.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.

2.18.3-beta7

  • Cache: the retry counter for an offering is now reset at the start of every construction round and after a successful load, instead of accumulating for the lifetime of the offering. Previously one short API disruption used up the whole allowance permanently, so from then on that offering got a single retry per round and was dropped again at the first hiccup.
  • Cache: an offering that fails to load moves to the back of the queue instead of being retried immediately, so a few problematic offerings can no longer consume the whole time budget while others wait.
  • Cache: fixed an off-by-one that made the plugin give up after four attempts instead of the configured five.
  • Tools: the hydration progress on Tools > Carta Online aanbod no longer counts abandoned offerings as completed, so the percentage reflects what is really in the cache. Note that offerings abandoned by an older version still count as completed until the next full construction round has run.
  • Provisioning: the webhook secret is now also created when the plugin is updated in place, not only when it is activated. WordPress does not run the activation hook on an update, so updated sites previously ended up without a secret: every webhook delivery was rejected and the offer cache refreshed only through the periodic construction. Existing sites without a secret get one automatically on the first request after this update, including an unattended overnight auto-update.
  • Provisioning: the plugin now verifies that its database tables were really created before recording the schema version, retries every 15 minutes while they are missing, and shows an admin notice explaining the cause. Previously a database user without the CREATE privilege produced a silently empty offer list that was never retried. Cache schema 1.3.2, which changes no table but makes every existing install run this verification once so sites that are already in that state are detected.
  • Provisioning: a plugin update is refused up front when the database user cannot create the cache tables, so the working version stays in place instead of being replaced by one that cannot fill its cache. WordPress applies this check before it touches any files, so nothing needs to be rolled back: the site simply keeps running on the version it has.
  • Provisioning: on sites with automatic updates enabled the plugin’s own automatic update is now skipped while that condition lasts, instead of being attempted and failing every night. An e-mail explains the cause and how to resolve it, and the update proceeds by itself on the next cycle once the database privilege is granted.
  • Provisioning: the update screen, the admin notice and the notification e-mail all explain how to recover, including the warning to overwrite the plugin rather than delete it when going back to an earlier version. Deleting runs the uninstaller, which removes the offering cache, the plugin settings and any claimed webhook subscriptions.
  • Settings: saving the settings no longer wipes the offer cache unless the portal address, API key or brand changed. Changing the update frequency, rendering or error settings now leaves the cached offerings in place, so visitors no longer see an empty offer list while the cache is rebuilt.
  • Security: API calls now validate the portal’s TLS certificate. Certificate verification was previously switched off, which meant the API key was sent over a connection that could be intercepted. Portals with a self-signed or expired certificate will now be refused until the certificate is fixed.
  • Uninstall: removing the plugin now also deletes the cron run history (co_cron_run_history) and any left-over local-cache lock options, so every setting the plugin writes itself is cleaned up on deletion.

2.18.3-beta5

  • Error handling: identical error e-mails are now throttled, so an outage (e.g. repeated cURL timeouts) no longer floods the admin inbox with the same message. Repeats of the same error are suppressed for 60 minutes (filter carta_online_error_email_throttle_minutes); errors are still written to the log every time, and the manual “Send test e-mail” button always sends.

2.18.3-beta4

  • Cache: fixed a failed schema migration that left the dynamic-items table on its old (Identifier, Name) primary key, so multi-value dynamic items (e.g. several Website_Capability values separated by “;”) stored only the first value. The migration now completes and existing offers are re-hydrated so all values appear.
  • Branding: fixed the offer reconciliation failing when a brand is configured. The v2 offer filter is now sent in the exact shape the API requires, so offers are correctly scoped to the configured brand when fetched.
  • Settings: saving one settings tab (Connection / Rendering / Error handling) no longer clears the fields of the other tabs.
  • Settings: fixed duplicate admin notices (“Settings saved” / “Cache cleared”) shown after saving.

2.18.3-beta3

  • Raised minimum required WordPress version to 5.3.
  • Compliance: resolved Plugin Check findings (WordPress coding-standards annotations for direct DB access on plugin-owned cache tables and a read-only nonce check). No functional changes.

2.18.3-beta2

  • co-test: in test mode the shortcode now reads live from the portal entered in the form (URL + API Key take precedence over the saved settings) instead of the local cache.
  • co-test: leaving both URL and API Key empty now falls back to the saved settings (runs against the configured portal) instead of refusing with a validation error.
  • Cache: default “local cache update frequency” is now 1440 minutes (once per day) and is shown in the settings field when the value is missing after an upgrade.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.0.
  • Portal URL: a trailing slash in the portal address is now accepted and normalised, so both https://host and https://host/ work.

2.18.3-beta1

  • Cache: multi-value dynamic items (e.g. Website_Capability) are now split on ; into one row per value, so a dynamic-filter on a single value matches offerings that list several capabilities. Schema 1.2.0 (surrogate Id primary key + UNIQUE(Identifier, Name, Value)); existing cached offerings are re-hydrated automatically on upgrade.
  • Cache: dynamic-filter shortcode now trims the filter key/value, so a stray space no longer breaks the match.

2.18.2

  • Search: [co-offerlist search=...] better wildcard use in URL based matching

2.18.1

  • Cache: dynamic-filter shortcode attribute (e.g. dynamic-filter="DetailPagina=/slug/") is honoured again. Each offering’s payload.dynamicItems is now flattened into a new junction table CartaOnline_OfferingDynamicItems (Identifier, Name, Value) so filters hit an indexed EXISTS clause. Schema 1.1.0 — every existing row is automatically re-hydrated on upgrade so the new table fills without operator action.
  • Search: [co-offerlist search=...] works again. Search terms wrapped in literal double quotes (the standard pattern emitted by carta_online_get_filter_from_url() and the ?s=... shortcode template) are now stripped before the SQL LIKE clause, matching the upstream API’s behaviour.
  • Renderer: %dyn_<KeyName>% placeholders are now wrapped in <div class="co-offer-dyn-<KeyName>">…</div> so themes can target individual dynamic items without parsing the rendered string. CSS class is sanitised via sanitize_html_class().

2.18.0

  • Admin: all plugin settings moved to a single tabbed page at Settings → Carta Online, with the tabs Connection, Rendering, Error handling, Carta Online Webhooks and Cron tasks. The three settings tabs share one option group and the active tab is carried through the save, so you stay on the tab you were working in.
  • Admin: new Cron tasks tab showing a one-line health badge, the last executed tasks and the scheduled tasks. Technical details (WP-Cron mode, drift, copy-paste system-cron instructions) sit in a collapsed section that only opens automatically when something needs attention.
  • Admin: cron runs are now logged (last 50 runs, with hook name, start time, duration and result) so a failing schedule is visible without server access.
  • Admin: the legacy top-level Carta Online menu was retired; the webhook subscriptions page now exists only as a tab on the settings page.

2.17.0

  • Cache: typed columns Status, DateStart, DateEnd, Location are now promoted from the primary instance of each offering, so shortcode filters like status=Open;AlmostFull match again
  • Added Tools → “Carta Online aanbod” admin page: live SyncState, searchable cache table, payload viewer, one-click “Wipe cache and reconcile now” button
  • Expertise list ([co-expertiselist]) now reads from the local cache (only fields that actually appear in offerings) instead of /stock/fields
  • Field filter is now case-insensitive so dynamic-fields cookies (lower-cased) match the cache’s canonical casing
  • Webhook subscriptions: only relevant slots (2 / 3) are listed; slot id detection now reads identifier (matches Carta API), claim/release flow works end-to-end
  • Webhook admin moved to Settings menu — fixes the 404 caused by hosting it as a submenu of the existing file-path menu slug
  • API Key field is now masked (type=password) on the Settings page
  • Single “Secret rotated…” admin notice instead of the duplicate it used to render
  • dynamicItems shortcode filter no longer throws — logged via carta_online_report_error and ignored, so pages keep rendering
  • cacheless_request now wraps array responses (e.g. /api/v1/webhook) in a {status, result} envelope; PUT/DELETE methods supported via wp_remote_request
  • Dutch translations added for every new admin string (Webhook subscriptions, Tools page, settings field labels)
  • Internal: shared co_localcache_promote.php helper used by both the drain (write side) and the repository (read side) so the typed columns and the rendered cards always agree on the primary instance
  • co-offerlist template now supports generic %dyn_<KeyName>% placeholders for every key in an offering’s dynamicItems object (T13469). Non-scalar values are skipped.
  • When the API rate limit (HTTP 429) is reached and exponential backoff is exhausted, an admin e-mail is sent (force-routed even when general error reporting is off, throttled to once per hour) asking to contact Carta support to raise the limit.
  • Instance promotion: dateStart/dateEnd/location are now correctly drilled out of instances[].planning[] (the OfferModel’s actual schedule layer) instead of instances[] itself, fixing missing locations on ClassMother/ClassSingle cards. Offerings with no scheduled planning render with empty location/date, which is the truthful representation — no sentinel substitutes.

2.16.0

  • Added local DB cache: offerings are now served from a WordPress-side store, refreshed continuously by webhooks (slot 3 / Synchronisation complete) and reconciled periodically as a backstop
  • Added Webhook subscriptions admin tab to claim / release slots and rotate the per-install webhook secret
  • Added realtime occupation overlay (js/co_realtime.js): cards stay rendered from the cache, only the live trainee count is refreshed via a single batched admin-ajax call
  • Added 429 / 5xx exponential backoff with jitter on every API call; web context is hard-capped at 1 s so live pages never block
  • Replaced deprecated get_page_by_title() calls with WP_Query (WordPress 6.2+ compliance)
  • All connection-affecting setting changes wipe the cache and trigger a fresh reconciliation; portal/key changes also release claimed webhook slots
